# [TASK] Tighten dependency/security-scan thresholds from critical-only to high+

## Task
#101 wired up OWASP Dependency-Check (backend) and npm audit (frontend/filmpire) at a deliberately conservative critical-only threshold (`failBuildOnCVSS = 9.0`, `npm audit --audit-level=critical`), since it's a brand-new gate on pre-existing dependencies. High-severity findings (CVSS 7.0-8.9 backend; "high" npm) currently pass through as report-only. Tighten both thresholds once the current backlog of high-severity findings is triaged, so this doesn't stay permanently lenient by default.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] Existing high-severity findings (backend OWASP report + `npm audit --audit-level=high` on frontend/filmpire) triaged: fixed, or suppressed with a real reason in dependency-check-suppressions.xml — backend: netty→4.2.16.Final, tomcat→11.0.24, jackson-2-bom→2.21.5, postgresql→42.7.13, log4j2→2.25.5, httpcore5→5.4.3, commons-compress→1.28.0, httpclient→4.5.14, springdoc→3.1.0 (patches swagger-ui's bundled DOMPurify); 2 confirmed CPE false-positives suppressed with documented reasoning (build-tool-only kotlin-stdlib via resilience4j-core, misidentified spring-boot-data-mongodb wrapper — real spring-data-mongodb resolves to 5.1.0, outside every affected range). Frontend: npm `overrides` for nth-check/svgo/serialize-javascript/underscore/postcss clears all 14 highs without a breaking react-scripts bump.
- [x] `build.gradle`'s `failBuildOnCVSS` lowered to 7.0
- [x] frontend-ci.yml's `npm audit` step raised to `--audit-level=high`
- [x] CI passes green at the new thresholds — verified locally: full backend build + test suite (274 tests across all modules) green, `dependencyCheckAggregate` green at 7.0 with only a below-threshold commons-jxpath finding (6.5, no fix exists) left as report-only; frontend `npm run build` + lint green, `npm audit --audit-level=high` exits 0 with only below-threshold moderate/low findings left (matching #101's already-documented no-safe-fix backlog)

## Estimate
**Hours:** 3

## Notes
Flagged by an independent review pass on #101 (2026-08-03): a threshold-tightening promise in a code comment isn't a tracked commitment. This issue is that tracking.

Turned out larger than the 3-hour estimate: today's NVD sync had already surfaced fresh critical CVEs (netty, tomcat, a build-tool-only Kotlin CVE) that were failing the build even at the old 9.0 threshold, on top of the expected high-severity backlog. Full triage in 3fae2ac.
